dish: Chef-cut A4–A5 kuroge wagyu, including rare cuts from whole-cattle buying, sliced to order from the counter showcase
n: Itamae Yakiniku Itto Tengachaya Honten (板前焼肉一斗 天下茶屋本店)
w: Butcher-backed 'itamae' yakiniku by Tengachaya where the chef cuts A4–A5 Japanese black beef to order from a glass showcase; a repeat Tabelog Yakiniku WEST Hyakumeiten pick (2020–2025) and an Osaka Metro NiNE spot.

dish: Takoyaki made with a 4-hour stock of chicken, bonito, kelp, vegetables and fruit — best eaten plain, or 'Young B' soy-mayo / goma-shio
n: Abeno Takoyaki Yamachan (あべのたこやき やまちゃん, Abeno)
w: Unassuming stall behind Abeno Harukas whose dashi-rich batter makes it, per Inside Osaka, 'probably the city's favourite place for takoyaki'; also picked by Mapple.

dish: Aged (jukusei) nigiri from fish bought direct from trusted fishermen at nearby Senshū ports — 'Osaka-mon' sushi
n: Osakamon Ryōri Sushi Moriya (おおさかもん料理 鮨 守屋, Sakai)
w: Sakai sushi counter aging local-port fish into 'osaka-mon' (Osaka-produce) sushi; in Time Out Osaka's 'South Osaka: 20 restaurants to go to' and the Sakai tourism bureau's 'experience South Osaka' feature.

dish: Kashimin-yaki — thin batter griddled with cabbage, chopped hen (kashiwa) and minced beef tallow; Yamato added the tallow and coined the name
w: Seaside Kishiwada teppan shop credited by Walkerplus with adding beef-tallow mince and naming 'kashimin-yaki', the city's soul food; also featured in JAL's OnTrip Kishiwada piece. (Street address conflicts between sources — Honmachi 4-4 vs 15-4 Kamiyamachi — so ward-level only.)

dish: Same-day Senshū catch sold by the fishermen's co-op; kaisen-don with house sauces and sushi lunch at the in-market eateries
n: Izumisano Fishermen's Co-op Aozora Ichiba (泉佐野漁協青空市場)
w: Co-op-run open-air fish market at Izumisano port, near KIX — Osaka's biggest-catch fishery selling the day's landing, with sushi and kaisen-don counters inside; picked by OSAKA-INFO and Walkerplus's Kansai-drive sushi-lunch feature.

dish: Showa-retro stall-street snacks — croquettes and yakisoba from the hand-built yatai
n: Shinsekai Market & Yatai-gai Food Stall Street (新世界市場屋台街)
w: 1916 covered market beside Tsūtenkaku, revived since 2022 as a cheap hand-built food-stall street by the shopping co-op's young members; featured by OSAKA-INFO (Shittonka/Discover Osaka local tour + spot page), Osaka Metro's Osaka Mania and Lmaga's Shinsekai night-market story. Closed Thursdays; hours vary by stall.
